prompt: The system $kx + 3y = 9$ and $2x + y = 5$ has no solution. What is the value of $k$?
hint: Picture the two equations as lines. Two lines share no point only when they run in the same direction without touching.

hints.text: Picture the two equations as lines. Two lines share no point only when they run in the same direction without touching.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try it on a known pair: $y = 3x + 1$ and $y = 3x + 7$ never meet, because the slopes match and the intercepts do not. Setting the two slopes equal is the whole technique.
Parallel lines have equal slopes. The first line has slope $-\dfrac{k}{3}$ and the second has slope $-2$, so set these two slopes equal.
Solving $-\dfrac{k}{3} = -2$ gives $k = 6$, and the constants still differ, so the value of $k$ is $6$.

learningObjective: Find the parameter that makes a system inconsistent.
explanation: For $Ax + By = C$ the slope is $-A/B$. The first line has slope $-k/3$; the second has slope $-2/1 = -2$.
Parallel lines have equal slopes: $-\dfrac{k}{3} = -2$, so $k = 6$.
Check that they are genuinely parallel rather than identical: with $k = 6$ the first is $6x + 3y = 9$, or $2x + y = 3$ — same slope as $2x + y = 5$ but a different constant, so they never meet ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Scale to match, then compare
steps: Multiply the second equation by $3$ so its $y$-term matches the first: $6x + 3y = 15$.
A system has no solution when the $x$ and $y$ parts are identical but the constants disagree, so $kx$ must equal $6x$.
That gives $k = 6$, and the constants $9$ and $15$ are different, so the lines are parallel and never meet.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: A sign slip when comparing the slopes $-\dfrac{k}{3}$ and $-2$ produces $k = -6$, which gives lines that cross once.
With $k = 6$ the first equation is $6x + 3y = 9$, which simplifies to $2x + y = 3$.
That has the same left side as $2x + y = 5$ but a different constant, so there is no solution and $k = 6$ is right.
